A photo released by Ecuador's Police Organized Crime Unit shows former presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez of the Citizens' Revolution party during her arrest on Thursday [AFP]By AFPPublished On 23 Oct 202623 Oct 2026
A judge in Ecuador has ordered that former left-wing presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez remain detained following her arrest for alleged money laundering.
The order on Friday came the day after 48-year-old Gonzalez, who challenged right-wing President Daniel Noboa in the 2023 election, was arrested in the rural town of Canuto.

Gonzalez, her party and her close ally, former President Rafael Correa, have called the arrest political persecution.
Several other members of Gonzalez’s Citizen Revolution (RC) party have also recently faced charges.
They include Guayaquil Mayor Aquiles Alvarez, convicted of illegally selling subsidised fuel and former Vice President Jorge Glas, serving a sentence for corruption.
Prosecutors have said that Gonzalez is one of seven people under investigation for financing the 2023 presidential campaign. The probe focuses on $500,000 poured into advertising during the race.
Gonzalez has denied wrongdoing, dismissing the charges as “absurd”.
Citizen Revolution President Gabriela Rivadeneira told a news conference on Thursday that Gonzalez’s arrest “confirms or makes visible what we have been saying lately: Ecuador is living under a dictatorship”.

Two former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agents have been charged in connection with a 2020 probe into a laptop belonging to former President Joe Biden’s son, Hunter Biden.
The former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, were charged with lying to Congress. They made their first court appearance in Washington, DC, on Friday.

A lawyer for Floris said she “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years”, while accusing the Justice Department of building its case on hearsay.
“Yet today, the DOJ [Justice Department] has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” the statement said.
“It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”

With just more than a week until the pivotal US midterm elections, the US Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit to block certification of the results in Alaska’s hotly contested Senate race.
In a lawsuit filed on Thursday, the Justice Department argued that an independent candidate with the same name as the state’s incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is currently running for re-election, is purposefully running to mislead voters.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Why do the US midterms matter for Trump and Congress?list 2 of 3‘Bordering on angry’: The state of play as US midterms enter final monthlist 3 of 3How the midterms could change Trump’s presidencyend of list
“Given the substantial likelihood that the inclusion of Daniel J Sullivan will confuse or mislead voters looking to cast a vote for Senator Sullivan, and thus distort the will of Alaskan voters, there is a substantial likelihood that a certification of the election will reflect an electoral process that lacked integrity,” the Trump administration’s filing read.
The Justice Department is asking a federal judge to delay certification to allow time for an investigation into “whether votes cast for Daniel J Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan”.
During a visit to Florida on Friday, Trump took credit for the lawsuit after reporters asked about it.
“I’m the one that said ‘do it,'” he told reporters in Fort Myers, Florida.
A Justice Department spokesperson did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Many people are feared to be trapped in Kenya’s capital, Nairobi, after a multistorey building under construction collapsed, leaving a huge mound of concrete as rescuers dig through the rubble.
The building came down on Friday at about 1pm local time (10:00GMT) on a busy commercial street in Eastleigh, a neighbourhood crowded with thousands of traders and residents.

Nairobi police chief Issa Mohamud said more than 10 upper floors were under construction. The ground floor had been rented to an electronics shop, a butchery and a grocery, according to The Associated Press news agency.
Al Jazeera’s Catherine Soi, reporting from Nairobi, said the developers and authorities are being asked “to answer now” as people were not supposed to be inside a building under construction.
She said rescue efforts were expected to continue through Friday night and Saturday.
Rescuers used poles stripped from trees and excavators to move concrete bound with steel, as heavy equipment was slow to arrive.Emergency personnel at the building collapse in Nairobi on Friday [Monicah Mwangi/Reuters]
Mohamud said one injured woman had been rescued and taken to hospital, while another person who had been calling for help had gone silent. He warned of a potential second collapse because the building was leaning on its neighbour.

Why are 40 cameras required?
Spain’s top-flight La Liga classifies matches involving Barcelona or Real Madrid as “Category A”, requiring at least 22 cameras for coverage.
Major matches like El Clasico or the Madrid Derby have a higher rating of “A+” and require 35 to 40 cameras distributed according to a pre-defined shooting plan, which includes their locations and coverage angles.
The details are made available to the referees’ technical committee and the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) technology team, advising them of the available image sources for reviewing refereeing decisions.

Kompany looks on during Bayern's 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League in Munich, Germany on October 21, 2026 [Leonhard Simon/Getty Images]By AFP and ReutersPublished On 23 Oct 202623 Oct 2026
Bayern Munich ⁠coach Vincent ⁠Kompany was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing during a training session, the ⁠German champions said.
The Belgian had been nursing a virus in recent days and had ⁠missed some of his team’s training sessions.
“On Friday, Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during a training session for Bayern’s reserve team,” the club ‌said. “The head coach of the professional squad had been observing the second team’s session.”
“Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in the hospital and will remain under medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff ⁠will manage all training and ⁠match-related operations.”
The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 at home against Arsenal in the Champions League earlier this week, are due ⁠to travel to Freiburg on Sunday.
“Vincent Kompany’s health is our top ⁠priority,” said Max Eberl, Bayern’s ⁠board member for sport. “At Bayern, we will do everything we can to ensure he makes a speedy recovery.”
“Vinnie is receiving ‌all the necessary medical care and support, and he will be given as much time ‌as ‌he needs. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a quick recovery.”
Kompany, a 40-year-old former Manchester City defender, had missed training and a news conference on Tuesday before the Arsenal game earlier this week.
“I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course, I didn’t listen to my body – and then at some point my body just said, ‘enough is enough!'” Kompany said after the Arsenal game. Advertisement

Consumers face high prices at the grocery store as inflationary pressures continue [File: David Zalubowski/AP]By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 23 Oct 202623 Oct 2026
Consumer sentiment in the United States hit a near-record low in the final reading before the consequential midterm elections as cost-of-living issues weigh on US consumers.
The University of Michigan’s Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped on Friday as continuing tensions between the US and Iran drove up prices at the grocery store and the petrol pump.
Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4US Social Security benefits to rise by 3.6 percent in 2027list 2 of 4How Iran messaging highlights cost of war ahead of US midterm electionslist 3 of 4Will Russia’s diesel shipment to the US lower prices before midterms?list 4 of 4Rising costs and tight budgets strain Americans ahead of midterm electionsend of list
The reading dropped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September, leading to the second-lowest reading on record. The lowest was only a few months ago in May, when it stood at 44.8 points.
The report measures how consumers feel about their personal finances at present and how they expect it will change over the next 12 months; whether they feel it is a good time to make major household purchases; and their expectations for the US economy over the next 12 months, as well as five years.
“Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy,” said Joanne Hsu, the director of the Surveys of Consumers. “Sentiment is now 10 percent below a year ago and 15 percent less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict.”
